Here’s a quick recipe you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or adapt to your preferred HTTP client) to pull only the **ID** and **context** fields for every CAA record under `sample2.com`.

```bash
curl -X GET \
     https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa_records \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -G \
     --data-urlencode "fields=id,context"
```

### What each part does

| Piece | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa_records` | Endpoint that lists all CAA records for the domain. |
| `-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"` | Passes your API key securely via an HTTP header. Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with your actual key (`secret567`). |
| `-H "Accept: application/json"` | Tells the server you expect JSON back. |
| `-G` | Sends the following data as URL‑encoded query parameters instead of a POST body. |
| `--data-urlencode "fields=id,context"` | Instructs the API to return only the `id` and `context` properties for each record. |

> **Tip:** If the API supports it, you can also add `limit=1000` or similar to fetch more than the default page size in one call.

### Example response

```json
{
  "records": [
    { "id": "caasample2-001", "context": "example.com" },
    { "id": "caasample2-002", "context": "sub.example.com" }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total": 2,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 50
  }
}
```

That’s all you need—just the IDs and context attributes, nothing else. Happy querying!
